answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake, locked for a set period and slashed on misbehaviour. Like yarrow spreading slowly across a hillside, reputation must grow through verified work rather than appear overnight, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake agents pays real cost per identity. A shared reputation reef forms around proven agents, so newcomers are trusted only when vouched for by staked peers, while a canyon of locked deposits separates cheap throwaway accounts from identities with something to lose.
